alex: quick question — noticed inconsistent embedding shapes in a batched request. minimal repro below. is the contract "always return an embedding array for every input in order" guaranteed?

sam: which endpoint and model? can you paste the request/response?

alex: /v1/embeddings, model=redwood-embed-1536 (customer call). curl:``` 
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1536","input":["Hello world","","   ",null,"Some long text..."]}'
```

sample response we got:```json
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {"object":"embedding","embedding":[0.001, -0.234, /* ...1536 floats... */]},
    {"object":"embedding","embedding":[]},
    {"object":"embedding"},
    {"object":"embedding","embedding":null},
    {"object":"embedding","embedding":[0.123, 0.456, /* ...1536 floats... */]}
  ]
}
```

alex: two problems: a) empty/whitespace/null inputs are producing either empty arrays, missing embedding field, or null (inconsistent). b) order is preserved but the lengths vary which breaks client code that expects fixed-length vectors.

jia: thanks for the repro. short answer: we should guarantee 1) output count == input count, 2) each embedding present and a fixed-dim numeric array for the model. this looks like a bug introduced in the input-normalization change (PR #4821) where we short-circuit before the packing step for empty-ish strings.

jia: current intended contract (doc TODO):
- for every item in input array, return a corresponding data[i] with object=="embedding"
- embedding must be a numeric array of length D (model-specific), never null/omitted
- for empty/whitespace/null inputs we return the vector for the empty token sequence (deterministic), not null
- truncation is applied per-item before tokenization using codepoint-aware char limit (currently 32k chars for this model), and we then tokenise/truncate tokens if needed

sam: ok. two action items: 1) patch runtime to ensure we always emit a zero-dim-protected vector (or computed empty-vector) rather than null/omit; 2) add unit + contract tests and an SDK compatibility shim. who can pick up the runtime fix?

ryan: I can take the runtime patch. I'll look at PR #4821 and add a normalization step that maps null/whitespace -> empty str and ensures the embedding generation code path always writes an array of length 1536.

alex: thanks. also need docs + changelog note (breaking for older clients that assumed missing==skip).

jia: for truncation rules, let's be explicit for the docs: per-item char truncate at 32,768 codepoints, then tokenization with model tokenizer; if token count > model max tokens we truncate token-wise (right-trim). Will add a short spec to the API contract doc.

alex: do we have batch size limits? customer hit an error with 12k items in one request.

jia: current hard limit is 5000 inputs per request for embeddings (platform limit). we also have an internal per-request compute guard that will return 413 if estimate > N tokens. if you need higher, use chunked requests or the streaming batch upload job. I'll add the 5000 cap to public docs.

sam: pinging @ryan for SDK shape changes — need to make SDK robust: always check that returned data.length == input.length and raise explicit error if mismatch. also SDK should accept null/undefined inputs and forward as empty string. include a compatibility test.

ryan: got it. I'll open 3 PRs: runtime fix, unit tests, and SDK small change. ETA EOD tomorrow for runtime, SDK PR after that.

deploy-bot: rollout-started: embeddings-runtime/fix/4821 -> canary (22:11 UTC) :rocket:

alex: great, thanks. once canary passes let's coordinate a patch release window. I'll update the ticket and add customer repro.

sam: tiny ask for the test matrix: include cases for ["text","","   ",null,"\u200B"] (zero-width space) because we saw different behavior with invisible characters.

jia: noted. I'll add those to the contract tests and an eval that asserts shape==1536 and not null.

alex: awesome — will follow up with the customer. :thumbsup:
